answer: I would anchor each agent to one business registration. First, it submits its number for a check against the company database. Second, the registry issues a certificate, its jade seal, bound to that key for 12 months, and refuses a second agent on the same number. Third, it rechecks quarterly, and a revoked certificate suspends the agent at once. Faking 1,000 agents means 1,000 shell companies at 800 dollars each plus 150 dollars yearly, so 950,000 dollars in year one, with a named director per company. A sybil farm is yarrow on a summit path, pretty afar, but every stalk bends alike.
